clue.text: It may wash dirty linen dramatically on the air

definitions.text: It may wash dirty linen dramatically on the air

parts.words: It may wash dirty linen dramatically on the air
parts.note: reads like a washing product, but describes a broadcast serial drama that airs characters' private scandals

explanation.definitionFit: A long-running radio or TV serial is built on characters' private scandals, publicly aired as drama.

clue.text: His money is well earned

parts.note: well earned sounds like praise for hard work, but means earned from a well, an oil well

explanation.definitionFit: Someone in the petroleum business makes his fortune from wells drilled for crude.

clue.text: What an expensive little parcel could cost

definitions.text: What an expensive little parcel could cost

parts.words: What an expensive little parcel could cost
parts.note: plays on the word meaning both a small parcel and, informally, a large sum of money, as in costing a fortune

explanation.definitionFit: A small wrapped parcel shares its name with the slang for a large sum, as in 'cost a fortune'.

clue.text: Father gets a fit of the sulks but a sweetie

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father
a pet is a fit of sulking, as in 'in a pet'

explanation.surface: Dad is in a bad mood, yet still a darling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a pet' is an old-fashioned phrase for being in a huff.
explanation.definitionFit: A term of endearment for a darling, especially a child.

clue.text: More mature port produced with energy in warm surroundings

indicators.note: the words are worked up or brought out in a new form, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A port wine that has aged well is served with vigour somewhere cosy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced' rearranges MORE MATURE PORT with E, the symbol for energy. The printed clue reads 'surroundings'; the file's 'surround, ings' is a scanning error.
explanation.definitionFit: The ambient warmth of an ordinary indoor space, the setting in which red wine is traditionally served.

clue.text: Weapon issued without charge to independent journalist

parts.note: something without charge is free
a lance is a long spear-like weapon

explanation.surface: Arms are handed out gratis to a self-employed reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: The original freelances were mercenary knights whose lances were free for hire.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer working for many publications on commission rather than on staff.

clue.text: Make sure as sure can be

parts.note: certain is a synonym of sure

explanation.surface: Check things to be absolutely positive.
explanation.definitionFit: To determine or establish something definitely, removing doubt.

clue.text: Poor winner, maybe, but a real sport

definitions.text: Poor winner, maybe, but a real sport

parts.words: Poor winner, maybe, but a real sport
parts.note: a poor winner sounds like a sore victor, but here means someone who does not win yet takes defeat graciously

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who accepts defeat graciously is a sportsman, even without the trophy.

clue.text: The others go into the Post Office quickly

indicators.note: one piece enters the other, so it sits inside the abbreviation

parts.note: PO is the abbreviation for Post Office
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: Everyone else heads into the post office in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: The file's 'Post Off' is a scanning error for 'Post Office'.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical tempo marking meaning very fast, also used as a conjuror's exclamation of speed.

clue.text: A pond looking horribly polluted in Lancashire

parts.note: filthy water looks black
a pool is a pond

explanation.surface: A filthy-looking pond somewhere in the north-west of England.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is a seaside resort town in Lancashire, a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous seaside resort on the coast of the north-west English county.

clue.text: Topping order to the ambitious teacher!

definitions.text: Topping order to the ambitious teacher!

parts.words: Topping order to the ambitious teacher!
parts.note: split as a two-word command, it urges a teacher to become the school's principal; whole, topping is slang for execution by decapitation

explanation.definitionFit: Topping is slang for execution, and cutting off the head is the classic order for it.

clue.text: Bess meant to emend the lowest of the stories

indicators.note: emending text corrects it by altering it, so these letters are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman named Bess intended to correct the final chapter of some tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stories' looks literary but means storeys of a building, as in American spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Floors of a building below ground level are its bottom levels.

clue.text: Military parade leaving an impression only skin-deep

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: an evening military display with music, and an inked design on the body.

clue.text: Solid preparation by the horticulturalist

parts.note: the phrase for hard groundwork is read literally as digging with a garden tool

explanation.definitionFit: Laborious groundwork, literally the digging a gardener does before planting.

clue.text: Pat and I heard assortment of popular songs

indicators.note: an assortment is a mixed collection, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Pat and I listened to a medley of chart music.
explanation.definitionFit: A weekly chart ranking the best-selling tunes of the moment.

clue.text: Had a celebration and got tipsy

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: celebrated festively, and became merry with drink.

clue.text: Electro-magnetic unit familiar to the ornithologist

explanation.definitionFit: The initials of an electromagnetic unit, and a large flightless Australian bird a birdwatcher knows.

clue.text: Fish given food additive by the Spanish

parts.note: E as in E-numbers, the codes for food additives
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Some seafood comes with a chemical additive from Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A long snake-like fish.

clue.text: Vessel in a Turner painting

indicators.note: the letters wanted are found in the middle of the artist's name

explanation.surface: A pot depicted in a work by the English landscape painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner is the English painter J.M.W. Turner.
explanation.definitionFit: A vase-like container, often for ashes.

clue.text: Tommy's usual habit is to get work outside the NHS

parts.note: a Tommy is a British private soldier
a practice is a habitual custom

explanation.surface: A soldier's routine involves earning money away from the health service.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy is old slang for a British soldier of the lowest rank. The NHS is Britain's state National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors' fee-paying work done independently of the state health service.

clue.text: One may meet him in a casual encounter

indicators.note: the man's name is found spanning the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone you might bump into by chance.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just 'him': a man's name, found across 'casuaL ENcounter'.
explanation.definitionFit: A short form of the male first name Leonard.

clue.text: Smart little flat returned to agent retirement on retirement

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'Smart little flat returned to agent retirement on retirement': 'retirement' is duplicated, likely an OCR error for 'Smart little flat returned to agent on retirement' (rev PAD + rev REP); no source confirms
annotationWithheld.clue: Smart little flat returned to agent retirement on retirement

clue.text: Dog seen to be reclining below a mountain-pass

indicators.note: in a down answer, the second piece is placed beneath the first

parts.note: a col is a pass between mountain peaks
to lie is to be reclining

explanation.surface: A sheepdog lies down beneath a high pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish sheepdog breed.

clue.text: Former Chancellor may have had a close shave in his shop

definitions.text: may have had a close shave in his shop

explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Barber was UK Chancellor of the Exchequer 1970-74; a men's hairdresser gives close shaves.

clue.text: Get the measure of a slightly larger dress

explanation.definitionFit: To assess someone, and to move to the next clothing measurement bigger.

clue.text: Looking all around while quietly cooking macaroni

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

indicators.note: cooking turns raw ingredients into something new, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Gazing about while softly preparing some pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking in a wide all-round view.

clue.text: The chap in charge of a bunker

definitions.text: The chap in charge of a bunker

parts.words: The chap in charge of a bunker
parts.note: a bunker read as a lair used in wartime, a ..., so the official in charge of it

explanation.definitionFit: An official responsible for supervising a place, like an air-raid shelter supervisor.

clue.text: Splendid Keep up the protest against tinned meat

parts.note: bully is old slang for splendid, as in 'bully for you'
a beef is a complaint or protest

explanation.surface: Bravo, keep complaining about canned food!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep up the' and 'against' only join the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Corned beef in tins, long a soldiers' ration.

clue.text: They're additional passengers

explanation.definitionFit: Clauses appended to a document or bill, and people travelling on a vehicle.

clue.text: Signal daily

explanation.definitionFit: To send a message by wire or gesture, and a national newspaper published every day.
